crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Credit Scoring with Alternative Data
children.blurb: Credit scoring with alternative data extends traditional credit bureau information to include rent payments, utility bills, bank account cash flows, telecom records, and e-commerce activity.

children.name: Covenant Extraction
children.blurb: Covenant extraction is the automated identification and structuring of contractual terms from credit agreements, indentures, and amendments.

children.name: Predicting Distress and Default
children.blurb: Predicting distress and default covers models that estimate the probability a corporate or sovereign borrower will miss payments, enter bankruptcy, or restructure, using financial statements, market prices, news, and alternative data.

children.name: Modelling the Yield Curve
children.blurb: Yield curve modelling in fixed income and credit risk concerns the term structure of interest rates across maturities, from overnight to long dated government and credit instruments.

children.name: Stress Testing Structured Credit
children.blurb: Stress testing structured credit means assessing how tranches of securitized products such as CLOs, ABS, RMBS, and CMBS would perform under severe economic and market shocks, including defaults, prepayments, spread widening, and rating migration.

sections.body: Fixed income and credit risk work uses machine learning to read and measure debt. AI now parses loan documents and bond indentures to pull out covenants, payment terms and triggers. Lenders and investors run models over alternative data, such as transaction records or shipping data, to estimate the chance a borrower will repay. Distress models scan financial statements, news and market prices for early signs of default. Yield curve models fit current bond prices to infer expected short term rates and term premia. Structured credit stress tests simulate how pools of loans or bonds would perform under economic shocks.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are routine and reliable, while others remain hard to validate. Covenant extraction from standard legal language is fairly accurate, but unusual clauses still need human review. Credit scoring with alternative data works best where there is a long, clean history of outcomes, and it can fail when the data drifts or when borrowers have thin files. Distress prediction flags many true problems but also produces false alarms, especially around sudden shocks that no historical model has seen. Yield curve modelling is well understood for liquid government bonds, but less so for corporate or illiquid curves. Stress testing structured credit depends heavily on assumptions about correlation and prepayment, which are hard to estimate honestly.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages move from a single borrower to the whole market. Credit Scoring with Alternative Data covers how models estimate an individual or small business borrower's risk when traditional credit history is missing. Covenant Extraction explains how AI reads loan and bond contracts to find restrictions and events of default. Predicting Distress and Default looks at the next step, using those borrower and contract signals plus market data to estimate failure. Modelling the Yield Curve steps back to the broad interest rate environment that prices all debt. Stress Testing Structured Credit then applies that environment and borrower level risk to portfolios of loans and bonds to see how they hold up under shocks.
